data.case_title: Suspicious Debt Collection Demand from EuroClaim Forderungsmanagement
data.explanation: This is a payment demand from a debt collection company (Inkasso) based in Cyprus, claiming you owe money for a "lottery club" telephone subscription (Gewinnspiel-Abonnement). The letter shows several classic signs of a scam collection notice: an unusually short 72-hour deadline, a demand to pay into a private individual's foreign account instead of a proper business account, threats of criminal prosecution for what would only be a civil debt, and a claim that objecting is "pointless." Do not transfer any money yet. First check whether you ever actually signed up for such a subscription, keep the letter and any related messages, and consider contacting the Verbraucherzentrale (consumer protection agency) or a lawyer before responding. Legitimate debts are rarely demanded within days, and you always keep the right to dispute a claim regardless of what the letter says.

data.summary: EuroClaim Forderungsmanagement Ltd., a debt collection agency registered in Cyprus, demands 287.40 EUR by 06.08.2026 for an alleged telephone-signed "Lotto-Muster-Club" subscription, threatening account seizure, a negative SCHUFA entry and criminal charges if unpaid. The letter shows multiple hallmarks of a scam collection notice (extremely short deadline, foreign personal-account IBAN, and discouragement from objecting).
data.title: Final Demand Before Seizure (Letzte Mahnung vor Pfändung) – Likely Scam Collection Letter
warnings: This letter shows multiple classic indicators of a fake/scam debt-collection (Inkasso) notice: an extremely short 72-hour payment deadline, demand for payment into a private individual's foreign account rather than a business account, threats of criminal prosecution for a civil debt, and a statement discouraging you from objecting.
The payee IBAN (LT71...) belongs to a private Lithuanian account and does not match the collector's stated Cyprus business address, which is unusual and suspicious for a legitimate company.
The claim that 'Ein Widerspruch ist zwecklos' (an objection is pointless) is a pressure/manipulation tactic; it does not remove your legal right to dispute the debt.
Do not transfer money or provide personal data based on this letter alone; verify the underlying claim (e.g. via Verbraucherzentrale or a lawyer) before taking any action.
